youtube_video.title: Zoho QuickBooks Integration: What Syncs and Which Way
youtube_video.description:
Read the full guide: https://zudoworks.com/insights/zoho-quickbooks-integration/

There is no single switch that connects Zoho to QuickBooks Online. Zoho has built a separate connection for each of its apps, and each one moves different records in a different direction. This 50-second explainer shows what Zoho CRM, Zoho Inventory, Zoho Billing, Zoho Expense, Zoho Analytics and Zoho Flow each sync with QuickBooks Online, and the rules to check before you connect anything.

Chapters
00:00 No single Zoho to QuickBooks switch
00:03 Zoho CRM: customers, vendors and products both ways
00:08 Estimates, invoices and purchase orders, read-only in CRM
00:14 Zoho Inventory and Zoho Billing send transactions out
00:20 Zoho Expense exports, Zoho Analytics only reads
00:26 One QuickBooks company per Zoho organisation
00:31 Tax rates must match exactly
00:36 Invoices from won deals: Zoho Flow, Deluge or a custom build
00:41 Read the full guide

Key facts from the guide
- Zoho CRM's native QuickBooks Online integration syncs contacts or accounts, vendors and products both ways. Estimates (Quotes in CRM), invoices and purchase orders arrive from QuickBooks as read-only records.
- Zoho Inventory and Zoho Billing send invoices, credit notes and payments to QuickBooks Online. Zoho Inventory also sends bills. The chart of accounts comes the other way.
- Zoho Expense exports approved expense reports as bills, journals or expenses.
- Zoho Analytics copies QuickBooks data in for reports and dashboards and changes nothing in QuickBooks.
- Each Zoho organisation links to one QuickBooks company, and the base currency must match. Zoho Inventory and Zoho Billing also need the same country.
- Tax rates are mapped and must match exactly. Map non-taxable lines to a zero per cent tax.
- To create a QuickBooks invoice when a CRM deal is won, use Zoho Flow (7 QuickBooks triggers, 17 actions), a Deluge function, or a custom build.

The guide also covers QuickBooks Desktop, Intuit's API limits, a checklist before you connect, and when moving the books to Zoho Books makes more sense.
